newsitem.title: UK: BT shares up on alliance hopes, "buy" advice.
newsitem.headline: BT shares up on alliance hopes, "buy" advice.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc rose in active trade on Thursday amid speculation that Spain's Telefonica de Espana SA may chose MCI Communications Corp as a U.S. partner.
Market sources said analysts at SocGen and SBC Warburg repeated strong "buy" advice on BT shares.

BT stock was up 10p at 443-1/2p by 1050 GMT. Over seven million shares had changed hands. "The shares are up on the hope that Telefonica will chose MCI and BT's life will become easier and AT&T's life more difficult," said one trader.

BT is planning to merge with MCI, the second-largest U.S. long distance carrier. The Financial Times newspaper on Thursday highlighted rumours that Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica may be about to choose MCI as its U.S. partner instead of global leader AT&T. Analysts at SocGen took the opportunity to repeat their "buy" stance. SBC Warburg were also positive on BT stock. "It does look as though Telefonica will chose MCI," said SocGen analyst John Tysoe. "This would secure MCI's position in South America and also put a huge dent in the Uniforce alliance," he said. "It would mean one of BT's major global competitors becomes weaker. Without a strong traffic flow out of Europe, AT&T has got a problem on the transatlantic route." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
